name: Sreemangal
summary: The tea capital of Bangladesh: endless green tea gardens, rubber plantations, lakes, a rainforest reserve and the famous seven-colour tea.
season_note: October to March is cool and dry. Rainy months are lush but roads can be muddy.
avoid_note: Hiking in Lawachara can be slippery after rain. Look out for leeches.

reach.how: Parabat, Jayantika, Upaban or Udayan Express from Kamalapur (check e-ticket)
reach.note: Comfortable and the most popular choice.

reach.how: AC coach from Dhaka (Sayedabad, Gabtoli) via Sylhet road

local.note: Hire for half a day to see tea gardens and Lawachara.

attractions.name: Lawachara National Park
attractions.what: A short trek through tropical forest to spot gibbons, langurs and many birds.
attractions.tip: Go early. Wear closed shoes. Hire a local guide.

attractions.name: Nilkantha Tea Cabin (seven-colour tea)
attractions.tip: Go in the afternoon; it can get crowded.

attractions.name: Tea gardens and Baikka Beel
attractions.what: Walk through tea estates and see the wetland bird sanctuary.
attractions.tip: Early morning mist is the best time for photos.

attractions.name: Madhabkunda Waterfall
attractions.what: The largest waterfall in Bangladesh, with a pool and a forest walk.
attractions.tip: Best from July to October. Take a hired car.

attractions.name: Lemon and pineapple gardens
attractions.what: Walk through the gardens and buy fruit directly from growers.
attractions.tip: Seasonal; ask your driver where to stop.

attractions.name: Khasi and Manipuri villages
attractions.what: Meet local communities and see handloom work.
attractions.tip: Be polite and ask before taking photos.

rules: Follow forest rules in Lawachara and keep your voice low.
Do not litter in tea gardens.
Carry insect repellent and wear shoes.
